title: The Haunting of Hill House
author: Shirley Jackson
setting: Hill House, an old mansion in the hills outside the village of Hillsdale
summary: Dr. John Montague, a scholar of the supernatural, rents a mansion with a dark reputation and invites people who have brushed against the unexplained. Only two guests come: Eleanor Vance, a lonely woman who spent eleven years caring for her mother, and Theodora, a bright and teasing artist. Luke Sanderson, the heir to the house, joins them. At night something pounds on the doors, cold spots fill the hallways, and messages appear on the walls asking Eleanor to come home. The others grow worried as Eleanor begins to feel that the house wants her to stay.
ending: The doctor decides Eleanor must leave for her own safety and sends her away. Speeding down the long drive, she wonders why no one is stopping her, then turns the wheel and crashes into the great oak tree at the bend.
note: The best opening paragraph in American horror. Read it out loud at the register and see who stops.

title: Dracula
author: Bram Stoker
setting: A castle in Transylvania, the seaside town of Whitby, and Victorian London
summary: Told entirely through letters, diary entries, telegrams, and newspaper clippings. Young solicitor Jonathan Harker travels to a castle in the Carpathian Mountains to help a count buy property in England, and slowly realizes he is a prisoner. The count sails to England, and soon Lucy Westenra grows pale and weak from a mysterious illness. Professor Abraham Van Helsing gathers Lucy's suitors, Jonathan, and his wife Mina to hunt the vampire through London, sterilizing his boxes of earth with holy wafers.
ending: The hunters chase the last box of earth back to the castle and catch the cart just before sunset. Jonathan cuts the vampire's throat and Quincey Morris stabs his heart, and the body crumbles to dust. Quincey dies of his wounds, smiling, as the red mark fades from Mina's forehead.
note: Not a single chapter is told by the vampire himself. That's why he's so scary.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
setting: Geneva, the university town of Ingolstadt, and the frozen Arctic sea
summary: The story arrives in the letters of an Arctic explorer, Robert Walton, who pulls a dying man off the ice. The man is Victor Frankenstein, a young scientist who built a living being from dead parts and fled in horror the moment it opened its eyes. Abandoned, the creature teaches himself to speak and read by spying on a poor family, and is rejected by every human he meets. He begs Victor to build him a companion. When Victor destroys the half-finished bride, the creature swears revenge on everyone Victor loves.
ending: Victor dies on board the ship while chasing his creation north. The creature comes to mourn over the body, tells Walton he will build his own funeral pyre at the top of the world, and drifts away on an ice raft into the dark.
note: Written by a nineteen-year-old on a rainy holiday as part of a ghost story contest.

title: Murder on the Orient Express
author: Agatha Christie
setting: The Orient Express, a luxury sleeper train stuck in a snowdrift in Yugoslavia
summary: Detective Hercule Poirot boards the crowded Calais coach of the famous express train from Istanbul. On the second night a snowdrift stops the train in the mountains, and in the morning a rich American named Ratchett is found stabbed twelve times in his locked compartment. With no police and no way off the train, Poirot interviews thirteen passengers from every corner of society. Every one of them has an alibi, and the clues point in too many directions: a scarlet kimono, a stopped watch, a burned letter about a kidnapped child.
ending: Poirot learns that Ratchett was the man behind the Armstrong kidnapping, and that nearly every passenger had a tie to the Armstrong family and struck one of the blows. He offers two solutions, and the railway director chooses the story of a stranger who escaped into the snow.
note: Perfect for a long train ride. Try to solve it before Poirot does.

title: Strangers on a Train
author: Patricia Highsmith
setting: A cross-country train, then Texas, Florida, and the suburbs of New York
summary: On a train heading south, the young architect Guy Haines meets Charles Bruno, a charming, drunk, idle rich man. Guy mentions he wants a divorce from his unfaithful wife Miriam. Bruno, who hates his own father, proposes a perfect plan: they swap murders, so neither killer has a motive the police can find. Guy laughs it off. Weeks later Miriam is strangled at an amusement park, and Bruno starts writing letters and showing up everywhere, demanding that Guy hold up his end of the deal.
ending: Worn down by threats, Guy kills Bruno's father and then cannot live with it. Bruno falls off a sailboat and drowns. Guy finally confesses to Miriam's former lover, not knowing that the detective Gerard is listening on the other side of the door.
note: Hitchcock filmed it a year later. The book is darker. Way darker.

title: The Girl on the Train
author: Paula Hawkins
setting: A commuter train into London and the suburban street it passes every day
summary: Rachel rides the same commuter train every morning and evening, even though she lost her job months ago. From the window she watches a young couple on their back deck and imagines their perfect life, naming them Jess and Jason. One day she sees the woman kissing another man. Soon after, the woman, really named Megan, goes missing. Rachel, who drinks heavily and has blackouts, was on that street the night Megan vanished, near the house where her ex-husband Tom now lives with his new wife Anna.
ending: Rachel's memory of the night finally comes back: it was Tom who hit her, and Tom who killed Megan. When he attacks her in the house, Rachel stabs him in the neck with a corkscrew, and Anna twists it deeper.
note: Three narrators, none of them reliable. Keep track of the dates at the top of each chapter.

title: Rebecca
author: Daphne du Maurier
setting: Manderley, a grand estate on the coast of Cornwall
summary: A shy young paid companion, whose first name we never learn, marries the wealthy widower Maxim de Winter after a whirlwind romance in Monte Carlo. At Manderley, his famous estate, she lives in the shadow of his first wife, the beautiful Rebecca, who drowned in a sailing accident. The cold housekeeper Mrs. Danvers keeps Rebecca's rooms exactly as she left them and tricks the new wife into wearing Rebecca's costume to the costume ball. Then a diver finds Rebecca's boat on the sea floor, with a body still inside.
ending: Maxim admits he killed Rebecca, but a doctor reveals she was dying of cancer and wanted him to do it, so the case closes as a suicide. Driving home at night, the couple sees a red glow over the hills: Manderley is on fire.
note: "Last night I dreamt I went to Manderley again." Start there and you won't stop.

title: The Shining
author: Stephen King
setting: The Overlook, a grand hotel high in the Colorado Rockies, closed and snowed in for winter
summary: Jack Torrance, a recovering alcoholic and failed teacher, takes a job as the winter caretaker of a mountain hotel, bringing his wife Wendy and five-year-old son Danny. Danny has the shining, a psychic gift that the hotel's cook Dick Hallorann shares and warns him about before leaving for the season. Snow closes the roads. The hotel's ghosts show Danny the bloody history of Room 217 and the topiary animals that move when no one is looking, while they slowly work on Jack, who forgot to vent the old boiler.
ending: Hallorann races back through the snowstorm to help. Jack, now fully controlled by the hotel, remembers the boiler too late, and it explodes and destroys the Overlook with him inside. Wendy, Danny, and Hallorann escape on a snowmobile.
note: The book ends very differently from the Kubrick movie. King still prefers his version.

title: Carrie
author: Stephen King
setting: The small town of Chamberlain, Maine
summary: Told partly through newspaper reports, scientific papers, court testimony, and memoirs written after the disaster. Carrie White is a lonely, bullied teenager raised by a fanatically religious mother. After a cruel scene in the school showers, she discovers she has telekinesis. Sue Snell, feeling guilty, asks her boyfriend Tommy Ross to take Carrie to the prom. Chris Hargensen, furious at being banned from the dance, plans a prank with a bucket of pig's blood above the stage.
ending: The bucket falls during the crowning. Carrie seals the gym and sets it on fire, then destroys much of the town, kills her mother, and dies in a roadhouse parking lot, with Sue feeling her final moments in her own mind.
note: King threw the first pages in the trash. His wife fished them out.

title: Mexican Gothic
author: Silvia Moreno-Garcia
setting: High Place, a decaying English mansion in the mountains of 1950s Mexico
summary: Noemi Taboada, a glamorous young socialite in Mexico City, gets a frantic letter from her newly married cousin Catalina, claiming her husband is poisoning her and that the walls are talking. Noemi travels to High Place, the crumbling mansion of the English Doyle family, a once-rich mining dynasty. The rules are strict: no talking at dinner, no smoking, no visits to town. The ancient patriarch Howard takes an unsettling interest in her, and only his shy son Francis seems kind. Mold creeps up the walls, and Noemi begins sleepwalking.
ending: Noemi learns the family's fungus lets Howard live on by taking over new bodies. She destroys the source hidden in the crypt, sets fire to High Place, and escapes down the mountain with Catalina and Francis.
note: Gorgeous dresses, rotting wallpaper. Ideal October book-club pick.

title: Station Eleven
author: Emily St. John Mandel
setting: Toronto and the shores of the Great Lakes, before and twenty years after a deadly flu
summary: On the night a famous actor dies of a heart attack while playing King Lear in Toronto, a flu pandemic begins that kills most of the world within weeks. Twenty years later, Kirsten Raymonde, who was a child actor in that play, travels with the Traveling Symphony, a troupe that performs Shakespeare and music for scattered towns around Lake Michigan. She carries two rare comic books called Station Eleven. In one town they run into a dangerous prophet who claims young wives and has ties to the actor's past.
ending: The Symphony reaches the Museum of Civilization, a small community living in an old airport. From an airport tower, Kirsten sees electric lights glowing in a town to the south, the first sign that the world is coming back.
note: A hopeful book about the end of the world. Yes, really.

title: World War Z
author: Max Brooks
setting: Every continent, during and after a global zombie war
summary: An oral history of the zombie war, told through interviews that a United Nations researcher gathered after it ended. A doctor in rural China treats the first infected boy. A smuggler profits from the panic. A soldier remembers the disastrous Battle of Yonkers, where tanks and missiles were useless against the dead. Governments hide the truth, then make brutal choices, like a South African plan to sacrifice part of the population so the rest can retreat to safe zones.
ending: The final interviews follow the world after victory is declared: armies still clearing zombies frozen in the snow, cities rebuilding, and survivors trying to explain what the war cost them.
note: Read it as a set of short stories. The audiobook has a full cast.

title: The Turn of the Screw
author: Henry James
setting: Bly, a remote country house in Essex, England
summary: A ghost story read aloud at a Christmas party from an old manuscript. A young governess takes a job caring for two orphans, Miles and Flora, at a country estate, under strict orders never to bother their uncle in London. The children are charming, but Miles has been expelled from school for reasons no one will explain. The governess starts seeing a man on the tower and a woman by the lake, and the housekeeper identifies them as the dead valet Peter Quint and the dead former governess Miss Jessel.
ending: Flora is sent away after a scene at the lake. Alone with Miles, the governess confronts him about Quint's ghost at the window, and he cries out. She holds him close, and realizes his heart has stopped.
note: Are the ghosts real? Critics have argued about it for a hundred and twenty years.

title: Bird Box
author: Josh Malerman
setting: A house outside Detroit and a river through the Michigan woods
summary: Something has come into the world, and anyone who sees it goes violently mad. Survivors cover their windows and go outside only with blindfolds. Malorie, pregnant when it began, found shelter in a house with a small group of strangers. Four years later she and two small children, called only Boy and Girl, row twenty miles down a river blindfolded, trusting the children's trained hearing, to reach a place that may be safe. Flashbacks show what happened to everyone else in the house.
ending: Wounded and exhausted, Malorie reaches the end of the river and finds a community at a former school for the blind, where people have survived safely all along. She finally gives Boy and Girl real names.
note: You'll want to close your eyes and listen to the room around you.

title: We Have Always Lived in the Castle
author: Shirley Jackson
setting: The Blackwood family house at the edge of a hostile New England village
summary: Eighteen-year-old Mary Katherine Blackwood, called Merricat, lives with her gentle sister Constance and their frail Uncle Julian in the family house. Six years earlier, the rest of the family died from arsenic in the sugar bowl at dinner, and Constance was tried and acquitted. The villagers hate them. Merricat protects the house with buried coins and nailed-up books. Then cousin Charles arrives, eyeing the family safe and trying to take Constance away.
ending: A fire breaks out, and the villagers who come to put it out smash the house instead. Merricat and Constance hide in the burned shell, living together in secret, while the guilty villagers leave food on their doorstep.
note: Merricat is one of the great narrators. Listen to what she doesn't say.

title: The Silence of the Lambs
author: Thomas Harris
setting: Quantico, a Baltimore hospital for the criminally insane, and a small town in Ohio
summary: FBI trainee Clarice Starling is sent to interview Dr. Hannibal Lecter, a brilliant psychiatrist and cannibal held in a Baltimore asylum, for help catching a serial killer the press calls Buffalo Bill. Lecter trades clues for stories from Clarice's childhood, including the night she tried to rescue a lamb on her cousin's farm. When a senator's daughter is kidnapped, the clock starts. Lecter is moved to Memphis and stages a bloody escape.
ending: Following a clue about a dressmaker, Clarice knocks on the killer's door alone. She chases Jame Gumb through his dark basement while he watches her with night-vision goggles, and shoots him when she hears his gun cock. Later, Lecter writes to ask if the lambs have stopped screaming.
note: Short chapters. You'll finish it in one weekend whether you planned to or not.

title: Something Wicked This Way Comes
author: Ray Bradbury
setting: Green Town, Illinois, in the last week of October
summary: Two thirteen-year-old best friends, Will Halloway and Jim Nightshade, hear a train whistle at three in the morning and watch a strange carnival set up in a meadow. Cooger and Dark's Pandemonium Shadow Show has a carousel that can make you older or younger with every turn, and Mr. Dark, the Illustrated Man, wears every soul he has captured as a tattoo. The boys see too much and are hunted through town. Will's quiet, aging father, the library janitor, is the only adult who believes them.
ending: In the library, Charles Halloway discovers the carnival's weakness is laughter. He laughs in the face of the Dust Witch and Mr. Dark, kills Mr. Dark, and saves Jim from the carousel. Father and boys run off across the meadow together.
note: The perfect read for the week before Halloween. Bradbury's sentences are basically poetry.

title: Rosemary's Baby
author: Ira Levin
setting: The Bramford, an old apartment building on the Upper West Side of Manhattan
summary: Young newlyweds Rosemary and Guy Woodhouse move into a coveted apartment in a gloomy old building with a dark past. Their elderly neighbors, Minnie and Roman Castevet, are nosy but generous, and Guy, a struggling actor, suddenly lands a big role after another actor goes blind. After a strange night of dreams, Rosemary becomes pregnant. Minnie brings her daily herbal drinks, her doctor tells her to ignore the constant pain, and her friend Hutch dies after warning her about the building.
ending: Rosemary is told her baby died at birth, but she hears crying through the wall. Knife in hand, she finds the neighbors' coven gathered around a black cradle, and the baby has his father's eyes. In the end, she begins to rock him.
note: A New York horror story. You'll look at your neighbors differently.
